source: Muse recheck of first-pass flags; apply through the belt (02 fact block -> 16 -> 04/05 remint), never in place

corrections.corrected_statement: Level two requires no violations, at fault crashes or suspensions for the ninety days before application, while Level three requires holding Level two for at least six months and driving twelve consecutive months without a moving violation, an at fault crash, a license suspension or a violation of Graduated Driver Licensing restrictions.
corrections.note: Level 3 needs six months on Level 2 plus twelve clean driving months, not twelve months all on Level 2.

corrections.corrected_statement: The Segment 1 and Segment 2 driver education state exams share the same minimum score of 70 percent.
corrections.note: Segment 2 seventy percent score is stated on page 19, not page 18.

corrections.corrected_statement: Adults must practice at least 30 days on a TIP before the skills test, a count of days, whereas the teen log counts supervised hours.
corrections.note: Teen supervised hour requirement is stated on page 19, not page 20.

corrections.corrected_statement: A change of address submitted online will update your drivers license or state identification card and your voter registration and will give you the opportunity to update the address for vehicle records connected to your account.
corrections.note: Corrected to show vehicle records are an opportunity to update, not automatic.

corrections.corrected_statement: Inside a roundabout stay to the right of the center island and yield to vehicles already in the roundabout, stopping only when it is the only way to safely avoid a collision or other danger.
corrections.note: Added missing or other danger exception to the stopping rule.

corrections.corrected_statement: If a train is coming, stop no closer than fifteen feet and no farther than fifty feet from the tracks, and trains overhang the tracks by at least three feet on each side.
corrections.note: Removed unsupported causal link between stopping distance and overhang.

corrections.corrected_statement: A fast vehicle's wind blast can startle a rider or push them off balance, raising the chance of a crash.
corrections.note: The wind-blast cause is stated on page 69, not page 70.

corrections.corrected_statement: In a roadside emergency the safest choice is generally to stay in the car with your seat belt buckled until help arrives.
corrections.note: Statement is correct but completes on the next page.

corrections.corrected_statement: If someone suspicious approaches your car, drive away or sound the horn, stay inside with doors locked, and call for help by mobile phone, which Michigan law allows for emergencies.
corrections.note: Drive-away instruction is on the previous page.
